name: Starter: West Frisian
about: West Frisian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Frisian order.

words.wêze: be (is: is, bin: am, binne: are)
words.hawwe: have (haw: I have, hat: has, hasto: have you)
words.kinne: can, be able to (kinsto: can you)
words.ite: eat (yt: eat, iten: eaten; te iten: to eat)
words.do: you (to a friend; dy: you as the object)

items.text: In tee en in wetter, asjebleaft.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: In tee en wetter in, asjebleaft.
In en tee in wetter, asjebleaft.

items.text: Hallo! Hoe is it mei jo?
wrong: Hallo! Hoe it is mei jo?
Hallo! Hoe mei jo it is?

items.text: Ik haw in broer en in suster.
items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
wrong: Ik hawwe in broer en in suster.
Ik in broer en in suster haw.

items.means: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?

wrong: Ik wol asjebleaft in wetter in.

items.text: Ik wenje yn in lyts hûs.
items.means: I live in a small house.
wrong: Ik wennet yn in lyts hûs.
Ik yn in lyts hûs wenje.

items.text: Myn mem giet nei de stêd.
items.means: My mother goes to the city.
wrong: Myn mem gean nei de stêd.
Myn mem giet nei it stêd.

items.text: Myn mem wurket yn it sikehûs.
items.means: My mom works at the hospital.
wrong: Myn mem wurkje yn it sikehûs.

items.text: De kat sliept op myn bêd.
items.means: The cat sleeps on my bed.
wrong: It kat sliept op myn bêd.

items.text: Ik stean alle moarnen om sân oere op.
items.means: I get up at seven every morning.
wrong: Ik opstean alle moarnen om sân oere.

items.text: Wy ite jûns om seis oere.
items.means: We eat at six in the evening.
wrong: Wy yt jûns om seis oere.

items.means: Do you have to work today?

items.text: Ik woe graach in glês wetter, asjebleaft.
items.means: I'd like a glass of water, please.
wrong: Ik graach wolle in glês wetter, asjebleaft.

items.text: Wy hawwe hjoed in koeke bakt.
wrong: Wy hawwe hjoed in koeke bakke.

items.text: Ik haw juster yn in restaurant iten.
items.means: I ate in a restaurant yesterday.
wrong: Ik bin juster yn in restaurant iten.

items.text: Wy geane mei de trein nei Grins.
items.means: We're taking the train to Groningen.
wrong: Wy giet mei de trein nei Grins.

items.text: Moarn gean ik nei de stêd.
wrong: Moarn ik giet nei de stêd.

items.text: Ik bin mei de fyts nei it wurk gien.
items.means: I rode my bike to work.
wrong: Ik bin mei de fyts nei it wurk gean.

items.text: Kinne jo my de wei wize?
items.means: Can you show me the way?
wrong: Kinne jo my de wei wiist?

items.means: Excuse me, do you speak English?

items.text: Is der in bus nei it stasjon?
items.means: Is there a bus to the station?
wrong: Is it in bus nei it stasjon?

items.text: Der binne trije winkels yn ús doarp.
items.means: There are three shops in our village.
wrong: Der hawwe trije winkels yn ús doarp.

items.text: De film fangt om acht oere oan.
wrong: De film oanfangt om acht oere.

items.text: It is tiid om te iten.
wrong: It is tiid om te yt.

items.text: Juster binne wy nei Ljouwert gien.
wrong: Juster wy is nei Ljouwert gien.

concept.line: A verb's ending changes with who does it: ik wurkje (I work), do wurkest (you work), hy wurket (he works), wy wurkje (we work).
A yes-or-no question starts with its verb, and after a question word the verb comes next; do can join the verb as -sto, -ste or -st: Hasto bern?
my is myn, your dyn and our ús, the same before every noun: myn mem (my mom), ús hûs (our house).
A singular noun takes de or it for the, every plural takes de, and a is in: de kat (the cat), it hûs (the house), in hûs (a house).
To someone you don't know, you is jo, with the verb's plural form: Wêr wenje jo?

words.means: gean = go; geane = go; giet = goes

concept.line: With wolle (want), kinne (can) or moatte (must), the second verb goes to the end, with no word for to: Ik wol Frysk leare (I want Frisian learn).
